# Teradata error codes — what each message actually means, and what to do

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/render_references.py from scripts/data/error_codes.yaml. Do not edit by hand. -->

Purpose: the error-code companion to `teradata-sql`; look a code up here before changing a statement, and quote the code and message verbatim when reporting to the user.

33 confirmed codes and 10 reported-but-unverified codes, from `scripts/data/error_codes.yaml`. The same file drives the plugin's PostToolUse coaching note, so the two never disagree. Text authored from Teradata documentation is marked as such in the source file (from Teradata documentation; verify against your release).

How to read a Teradata error:

- The code is stable across releases; the message text is what tells you which case you hit.
- Fix exactly the named defect, re-run once, and stop after two retries.
- On 5628 / 3810 / 3807, discover the real name with `base_tableDDL` or `base_tableList` in the same turn before retrying.
- Messages that read like syntax (3541) or like a missing object (3802 after a failed CREATE) often mean space.

## Confirmed codes

Message text verified against Teradata documentation or a real message captured on a live system.

### SQL dialect, objects and types

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2616 | `Numeric overflow occurred during computation` | The result type is too narrow for the value — a small DECIMAL precision, or DECIMAL arithmetic inside a statistic such as STDDEV_POP or a wide SUM. | Use DECIMAL(18,2) for money and totals, and CAST the inputs of statistical functions to FLOAT before computing. | `teradata-sql` |
| 2666 | `Invalid date supplied` | A string cast to DATE is not a plain YYYY-MM-DD — it carries a time component or a non-date value. | Use TRYCAST(SUBSTRING(col FROM 1 FOR 10) AS DATE) on string timestamps and count the NULLs it produces. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3504 | `Selected non-aggregate values must be part of the associated group` | A column in the select list is neither aggregated nor listed in GROUP BY. | Add the column to GROUP BY (positional GROUP BY 1, 2 is fine) or wrap it in an aggregate. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3706 | `Syntax error` | The parser found a token where a data type, keyword or name was required — an alias inside CAST, LIMIT/FETCH FIRST, an alias with a space, a missing parenthesis — or the text names a feature that is not enabled on this system. | Fix the named token — close CAST(... AS <type>) before the alias, use TOP/QUALIFY instead of LIMIT — or read the rest of the message for the disabled feature. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3707 | `Syntax error, expected something like` | A lexical problem — a reserved word used as an alias, VARCHAR without a length, comma-form SUBSTRING, or a function that does not exist in Teradata (MONTH(), YEAR(), DATEDIFF). | Rename the alias, add the VARCHAR length, use SUBSTRING(col FROM 1 FOR n), and use EXTRACT/ADD_MONTHS for date parts. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3760 | `String not terminated before end of text` | A single-quoted string literal was never closed, often because an embedded quote was not doubled. | Close the literal and write embedded quotes as two single quotes ('O''Brien'). | `teradata-sql` |
| 3771 | `Illegal expression in WHEN clause` | A subquery (x IN (SELECT ...)) appears inside a CASE WHEN, which Teradata does not allow. | Move the test to a scalar subquery in the select list or a LEFT JOIN with an IS NULL check. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3802 | `Database` | The database named in the statement does not exist on this system — a typo, the wrong system, or a CREATE DATABASE that failed earlier without being noticed. | Confirm the name with base_databaseList; if it should exist, check the parent's PermSpace for a swallowed 3541. | `explore` |
| 3803 | `already exists` | A CREATE ran against an object name that already exists in that database. | Use a deterministic name and DROP-then-CREATE (ignoring 3807 on the DROP), or pick a new name; never loop on random names. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3807 | `Object` | No object with that name exists in the database the statement resolved it to — an unqualified name, a typo, or a name that changed between the steps of a task. | Qualify every reference as <db>.<table>, confirm with base_tableList, and reuse one deterministic name across steps. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3809 | `is ambiguous` | The column exists on more than one table in the join and was referenced without a table alias. | Alias every table and qualify the column (t.status); never use JOIN ... USING. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3810 | `Column/Parameter` | The column or parameter does not exist on that table, view or macro. | Call base_tableDDL or base_columnDescription on the object in the same turn, then retry with the real name. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3822 | `Cannot resolve column` | A bare column name cannot be matched to any table in the FROM clause — usually a JOIN was dropped or the column lives on a table you did not join. | Qualify the column with its table alias and add the missing JOIN. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3853 | `is not a table` | SHOW TABLE (what base_tableDDL runs) was pointed at a view or other non-table object. | Use SHOW VIEW <db>.<view> via base_readQuery, or HELP TABLE for the column list. | `explore` |
| 5404 | `Datetime field overflow` | A datetime component does not fit the target type — most often microseconds into TIMESTAMP(0), sometimes an out-of-range value from an external source. | Truncate fractional seconds before the insert or declare TIMESTAMP(6); on external reads, project explicit columns and CAST them. | `teradata-sql` |
| 5407 | `Invalid operation for DateTime or Interval` | A string operation (SUBSTRING, LIKE, concatenation) was applied to a real DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP or INTERVAL column. | Use CAST(col AS DATE) or TO_CHAR/EXTRACT on typed columns; reserve SUBSTRING for string-typed dates. | `teradata-sql` |
| 5628 | `not found in table` | The column does not exist on that table. | Call base_tableDDL on the table in the same turn and retry with a column that exists; never guess a second name. | `teradata-sql` |
| 6706 | `The string contains an untranslatable character` | Text containing a character outside the LATIN repertoire (em-dash, curly quotes, NBSP, non-Latin scripts) was written to a LATIN column or session. | Declare the column CHARACTER SET UNICODE, or fold the text to Latin before the write. | `teradata-sql` |
| 6916 | `TOP N Syntax error` | TOP n was combined with DISTINCT, QUALIFY, SAMPLE or a WITH ... BY subtotal clause in the same SELECT; the message names which one. ORDER BY with TOP is allowed. | Use only one of them. For top-N prefer QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...) <= n on its own, since it composes with GROUP BY and window functions; keep TOP only by moving the DISTINCT, SAMPLE or WITH clause into a derived table and applying TOP outside it. | `teradata-sql` |
| 7453 | `Interval field overflow` | An INTERVAL value did not fit a DECLARED INTERVAL type — a column, parameter or CAST target whose leading precision defaults to 2 digits. It is NOT caused by a wide INTERVAL literal; a literal is sized from its own digits up to 4, so `INTERVAL '365' DAY` computes correctly and five or more digits raise 3706 instead. | Widen the declared target — `CAST(x AS INTERVAL DAY(4))` — or use integer-day arithmetic on a DATE. | `teradata-sql` |

### Space and capacity

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2644 | `No more room in database` | The named database has no PERM left; when the database is DBC, the transient journal cannot grow and every data-writing statement on the system fails. | For DBC, purge the pure log tables (ResUsage*, EventLog, SW_Event_Log, TDWMSummaryLog) per the health skill; for a user database, raise its PERM or remove data. | `health` |
| 3541 | `The request to assign new PERMANENT space is invalid` | The parent database does not have the requested amount of unallocated PERM — the message reads like syntax and means "no room". | Check PermSpace on the PARENT in DBC.DatabasesV, then MODIFY DATABASE <parent> AS PERM = n or request less. | `health` |

### Rights, ownership and proxy connections

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3523 | `does not have` | The session user lacks the named right on that specific object; a grant on the parent database does not cascade to a child database created later. | Grant the right on the database or object actually read, then verify with sec_userDbPermissions. | `health` |
| 3524 | `does not have CREATE TABLE access to database` | The user cannot create tables in that database — always true for DBC, for everyone. | Point the CREATE (or a vector-store target_database) at a normal working database. | `vector-store` |
| 5315 | `does not have SELECT WITH GRANT OPTION access` | The view's owner (the database that contains the view, not the connected user) lacks SELECT WITH GRANT OPTION on an object the view references. | GRANT SELECT ON <source_db> TO <view_db> WITH GRANT OPTION, then re-create the view. | `health` |

### Native Object Store (NOS) and authorizations

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4969 | `Couldn't resolve host name` | The external object store in a LOCATION or WRITE_NOS call could not be reached — a bucket.host path shape, a wrong endpoint, or an HTTPS attempt against an HTTP endpoint (the same code carries "SSL connect error" / "SSL wrong version number"). | Use a path-style LOCATION ('/s3/<host>/<bucket>/'), confirm the endpoint, and match the scheme (HTTP vs HTTPS) to the store. | `archive` |
| 6881 | `Only Simplified Authorization object is allowed` | WRITE_NOS was given a TRUSTED/DEFINER authorization; it accepts only a simplified AUTHORIZATION object. | Create a second, simplified AUTHORIZATION over the same credentials for WRITE_NOS; keep the trusted one for CREATE FOREIGN TABLE. | `archive` |
| 6938 | `does not exist` | The AUTHORIZATION object named in the statement does not exist in the database where the object resolves it — for a deliberately bogus name this is the expected result and proves the feature is enabled. | Create the authorization in the same database as the foreign table, or read it as a positive enablement signal when probing. | `archive` |
| 6953 | `does not match` | The authorization's definition (kind or security type) does not match what the statement requires — a simplified authorization passed where a TRUSTED one is needed, or the reverse. | Use the trusted authorization (unqualified name) for CREATE FOREIGN TABLE and the simplified one (db-qualified) for WRITE_NOS. | `archive` |

### Open table format (Iceberg) and datalakes

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5589 | `Function` | The referenced system function (for example TD_ICEBERG_READ) is not installed — open table format support is absent on this system. | Install and enable the OTF feature per the archive skill's enablement reference before retrying. | `archive` |
| 7825 | `in UDF/XSP/UDM` | An external routine (the OTF connector) raised an error; the text after SQLSTATE is the real cause — "Table was created concurrently" is a catalog version-skew defect, and dropping a non-existent OTF table also surfaces as this code rather than a clean 3807. | Read the SQLSTATE text; tolerate it on idempotent pre-drops; treat the "created concurrently" form as a catalog/version problem, not a retry candidate. | `archive` |

### Connection and transport

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8017 | `The UserId, Password or Account is invalid` | The logon itself was refused. The database is up and reachable — it answered — so this is a credential, not a network or health problem. A wrong password, a wrong LOGMECH (TD2 vs LDAP), a locked or expired account, or a DATABASE_URI whose user is not the one you think all produce it identically. | Re-check the user and password in the credential source the doctor reports (plugin option, DATABASE_URI, or the 0600 teradata.env), and confirm LOGMECH matches how the account authenticates. Never paste the connection string into the conversation to check it. | `setup` |

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5148 | `crashcode 5148` | An AMP is crashing while writing the system event log (seen in the node's system log as "AMP n crashcode 5148 on DBC.SW_Event_Log"); if it recurs during startup recovery no session can ever be established. | Follow the teradata-recovery triage — test with logons disabled before attempting any SQL remedy; requires OS access to the Teradata node. | `teradata-recovery` |

## Reported but unverified

These codes were observed on live systems, but the message text below was not verified against Teradata documentation or a captured message. Treat the fragment as a hint, read the real message when you meet it, and verify against your release.

### SQL dialect, objects and types (unverified)

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3532 | `Conversion between BYTE data and other types is illegal` | A BYTE/VARBYTE value (typically the output of HASHROW) was CAST or compared to a numeric or character type. | Use HASHBUCKET(HASHROW(...)) for an INTEGER, or FROM_BYTES(HASHROW(...), 'base10') for a number; never CAST(HASHROW(...) AS BIGINT). | `teradata-sql` |
| 3535 | `A character string failed conversion to a numeric value` | A string literal was compared to or inserted into a numeric column — commonly '1' against a BYTEINT flag. | Check the column type; compare BYTEINT/INTEGER flags with unquoted 1/0 and VARCHAR flags with quoted '1'/'0'. | `teradata-sql` |
| 3654 | `Corresponding select-list expressions are incompatible` | The branches of a UNION/UNION ALL do not line up — a different column count, order or incompatible types (a SELECT * across a base table and a foreign or Iceberg table is the usual cause). | Project explicit columns in every branch and CAST the external side to the base table's declared types. | `archive` |
| 5612 | `already exists` | A CREATE DATABASE/USER/ROLE/PROFILE ran against a name that already exists. | Treat it as idempotent success when the existing object is the intended one; do not use it as a catch-all that hides 3541 (no space). | `health` |

### Rights, ownership and proxy connections (unverified)

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9203 | `CONNECT THROUGH` | A proxy connection (SET QUERY_BAND ... PROXYUSER) was attempted without a matching GRANT CONNECT THROUGH; there is no exemption for a user proxying as itself. | GRANT CONNECT THROUGH <trusted_user> TO PERMANENT <proxy_user>, or remove the PROXYUSER query band. | `setup` |

### Open table format (Iceberg) and datalakes (unverified)

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4893 | `PURGE` | DROP TABLE on an open-table-format table was issued without the required PURGE ALL / NO PURGE clause. | Write DROP TABLE <datalake>.<db>.<t> PURGE ALL (removes object-store files) or NO PURGE (keeps them). | `archive` |
| 7454 | `DateTime field overflow` | A microsecond TIMESTAMP read from an external table was CAST directly to TIMESTAMP(0). | Bridge through a string — CAST(CAST(ts AS VARCHAR(19)) AS TIMESTAMP(0)). | `archive` |
| 9134 | `VIEW` | CREATE VIEW over an open-table-format (Iceberg/Delta) table is not supported. | Federate hot and cold data with a UNION ALL query, not a view. | `archive` |
| 9723 | `TD_SNAPSHOTS` | The TD_SNAPSHOTS table operator was invoked with a column subset or COUNT(*); it supports only SELECT *. | SELECT * FROM TD_SNAPSHOTS (ON <otf_table>) AS d and filter/count in an outer query. | `archive` |

### Connection and transport (unverified)

| Code | Message fragment | What it actually means | Do this | Skill |

| 444 | `unable to connect` | The client never reached the database. A firewall that DROPS rather than rejects makes this hang until the timeout instead of failing fast, so a long pause before the error is the signature of a blocked port rather than a wrong host. | Prove reachability to port 1025 independently of the plugin before changing any credential; then re-run the doctor. | `setup` |
